svg.title: TOPAK C9 — A workflow is a promoted DAG: the promotion seats every cell, and the orchestrator only narrows
svg.desc: Until ADR-0054 a Run cell's work could not reach another cell: Run's ingress is a closed list and no item on it is another cell's output (finding 1). A workflow is a promoted graph of seatings. Its promotion is the grant of every lease it will issue, so no principal grants another; the mechanism routes on typed attributes it lifts; an orchestrator cell may only choose among edges the mechanism has already enabled, and its route is checked again where it is applied. ADR-0054 is Proposed and nothing here is in force: its ten dependent amendments are pending and not applied. The reference was built to it anyway and links its floor stage, which is not in force either (G11 §1.1, §2.5, item 102; ToO rev 15 §2.11).
svg.text: TOPAK · C9

text.tspan: A workflow is a promoted DAG: the promotion seats every cell, and the orchestrator only narrows

svg.text: Until ADR-0054 a Run cell's work could not reach another cell: Run's ingress is a closed list and no item on it is another cell's output (finding 1). A workflow is a promoted graph of seatings. Its promotion is the grant of every lease it will issue, so no principal grants another; the mechanism routes on typed attributes it lifts; an orchestrator cell may only choose among edges the mechanism has already enabled, and its route is checked again where it is

applied. ADR-0054 is Proposed and nothing here is in force: its ten dependent amendments are pending and not applied. The reference was built to it anyway and links its floor stage, which is not in force either (G11 §1.1, §2.5, item 102; ToO rev 15 §2.11).

text.tspan: Built at reference · on a floor not in force

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The run cell, the floor and the grant paths in force are G10's (G11 §2.2, §2.5). ADR-0054 was drafted on 2026.10.07 from a design discussion in which the custodian settled nine things, ⟨K1⟩ to ⟨K9⟩; every other choice is the drafter's. One author, one day, and the module is the drafter's as well (Consequences). Its ratification also waits on a reader who is not the drafter (§12; ADR-0029 A2).

The module's graph, drawn as its header draws it (Workflow.tla): s the one decision point, c outward, j the sink joined on any; lineages {A, B}, one seating that Alternates admits. A node is one round of one cell; its task is promoted text whose slots only a handle fills, so neither the orchestrator nor a worker writes a task (§1). Every edge is

computed or chosen, carries a guard and declares a delivery mode, clear or handle. The graph is acyclic, checked at load: a loop such as draft-and-review is unrolled into a fixed number of nodes, so termination is a property of the shape and a checker reaches every path; a graph with a cycle does not load (§1 ⟨K1⟩). A step bound and a time bound
T_wf bound the whole workflow, both placeholders (§1). At the reference the same shape runs end to end, with scripted cells (A16).
the promotion grants a lease
computed edge: the mechanism fires it
chosen edge: an applied Route takes it
Route: selects, only narrows
outward node

text.tspan: Why: every orchestration method in use chains agents by trusting something (Context)

svg.text: Pipelines, graphs, supervisors, handoffs, group chats, agent-as-tool and A2A each let one model's output steer what runs next, or hand a transcript on, or let an
agent call a subordinate with its own credentials. Against the havoc premise (ADR-0007) the survivors are those in which agents never address each other

text.tspan: and something that is not a model decides what runs next.

svg.text: CaMeL's split is kept and its trust removed: its planner "is trusted to write the plan". Here the plan is a promoted artifact, and what is left of the planner may only
choose among enabled edges.
The delegation gap closes in its cheaper form (gap row 1.3; external assessment §5 item 2), on ratification: a deployment that needs sub-agents seats each
one by promoting a workflow (§2).
The only clause that adds authority, and it adds none the quorum did not vote on. Every other clause the mechanism applies subtracts (status note).
Each lease is still granted, not merely activated: confinement is appraised at that grant with a nonce from the log (ADR-0034 §3), and the grant refuses as any
grant does. A refused grant fails the node; nothing grants it lower and no other seating stands in.
Subtractions reach nodes not yet started: a rules-epoch change voids every lease not yet issued, as it voids votes in flight (ADR-0024 §3); a revocation of a
principal, Persona or profile bars the leases that name it. The node fails and the workflow fails closed (§9).
Inside a workflow no operator makes successor grants; EndRound, Revoke and FenceEpoch still reach every cell (ADR-0050 §4; ADR-0031 A4). A principal
seated at several nodes holds one live lease, so its rounds are granted in log order.
ADR-0055 (Proposed) lets a workflow of kind mesh have cycles, under an activation budget the promotion votes on; the activation becomes the unit, and the
orchestrator holds no state (ToO rev 15 §2.11). Drawn in D6. The default kind stays the DAG drawn here.

text.tspan: §3 · Edges are computed or chosen, and the orchestrator only narrows (K5, K8)
Proposed · ADR-0037 A5 · ADR-0040 A2 · ADR-0043 A3

svg.text: orchestrator, Run only. ADR-0037 §4's table gains a sixth kind (drafter's choice: a new kind, so that B10 and the delivery table bind it by kind)
Route(edge) and Report. No Consult, no Actuate. A new floor forbid refuses Route from any other kind, and B10 already refuses it every authoring variant
edge names a chosen edge of the workflow the lease names, out of the decision point the round was granted for. No other argument ⟨K8⟩: tasks are templates, so there is nothing to bind

One round per decision point, granted by the promotion when the decision point is ready, ended when its Route applies or its lease lapses. Decision points are served in log order, since a principal holds one live lease (ADR-0031 §2) (drafter's choice)

The task, from the promotion; the decision point's enabled chosen edges, each with its target's interface (ADR-0048, from promoted text); the attributes its guards read, with their labels and the basis index (§8); and a handle for each output. Never bytes. Its
Listener's delivery table is a mechanism constant, not bundle data, so no bundle can deliver it anything in the clear
The task's label, and nothing else can enter it. R5 to R7 never bind it, because it has no Actuate
Are written to its round topic for its Observer, and are never an input to any node (§5)

A computed edge fires when its guard holds, evaluated by the mechanism inside the apply of the entry that made it evaluable: one evaluation, at one log position, no gap. A chosen edge leaves a decision point, a node with more than one chosen outgoing edge; when it is ready the guards of its chosen edges are
evaluated, and the orchestrator selects one among those whose guards hold. ADR-0043 A3 gives §2's Run table the row orchestrator: Route, Report; ADR-0039 A3 couples it as a Thinker is.
It cannot enable an edge whose guard is false, so every safety property must already hold for every enabled edge, whichever is taken. It affects how good the work is and never whether it is safe.

The safety argument needs nothing from the orchestrator: it is in the record for quality alone, which is why it is optional. A graph of computed edges is run by the mechanism alone and has one Byzantine principal
fewer (drafter's choice: a load check, not a judgment of necessity).

A typed record on the orchestrator's round topic, admitted and ordered; the grant it leads to is the promotion's (§2). Effects stay {tool invocation, principal emission}; authority changes stay {promotion, anchor
issuance}. ADR-0040 A2: "exactly three variants" reads "exactly four".

Finding 3, the doubt: Route strains the enumeration. It is ordered and recorded like an emission, and its consequence is a grant. A C2 reviewer may read it as a third kind; that is ADR-0015's C2 question.

text.tspan: §4 · Attributes are lifts, and guards read only what is settled (K6, K7)

svg.text: How the round ended: outcome, expired, fenced, revoked
actuates, denials ⟨R6⟩
Counts A count ⟨R6⟩, bounded by the round bound R
The worker's clearSet at its seal
Its cell Observer has reported coverage to the seal (§7)
A finding has been ordered against the round. The one attribute that changes after the end, and only from false to true
A value from the node's closed enum, declared in the workflow, taken from the typed outcome field of the worker's Report; none if none was made
A handle on the node's Reports, labelled as §5 says

Struck as the record strikes them ⟨R6⟩: denials was dropped on 2026.10.09 by the custodian's decision. It had no replicated source: a denial is written to the round topic by the replica that refused it and is never ordered (ADR-0015; ADR-0051 §5), so no replica holds a count

every replica agrees on; R bounds admits, not denials; and the count was the worker's to choose, by making requests it knew would be refused. Denials stay on the topic for the Observer and the correlator, outside any guard. ADR-0047 A1 drops the word; at the reference, A17 (
749d54f; mechanism/ finding 22, where the reference had lifted 0).

Lifted by the mechanism in one log entry when a node's round ends: a fixed set, never declared by policy (ADR-0047 R13), none of them a literal ⟨K6⟩. A syntactic lift fixes an attribute's form, not its honesty: observed attributes are facts no principal chose; outcome is
chosen by a Byzantine worker, and §5's routing rule is what bounds that choice. Guards should prefer observed attributes. Policy reads none of them (ADR-0047 A1).
A predicate in a fixed, decidable language: equality and set membership over enums and labels, comparison of
bounded counts with constants (after R6, actuates alone), and the connectives.

text.tspan: No strings, no arithmetic, no temporal operator.

svg.text: The mechanism evaluates guards; they are not policy (drafter's choice), so they are among the mechanism checks
ADR-0033 §4 re-runs at apply (§8). Guards as Cedar, re-checked by freezing their input, was not taken: two
mechanisms where one does (Options).

text.tspan: Settled guards: the source and its dominators (§4)

svg.text: A guard reads only the attributes of the edge's source and of the nodes that dominate it, those on every path from
the root to the source. They have all ended before the source is ready, so the set is settled when the guard is first
evaluable. A join on any cannot read a branch that may still be running.
Every attribute but found is written once, and found only subtracts, so a guard's value cannot change after it is first
evaluable except towards disabled. §8 rests on that (finding 4).

text.tspan: A node's round may end on its outcome (§4; ADR-0042 A3)

svg.text: Run has no terminal variant (ADR-0040 §4). Here the admit of a Report carrying outcome ends the worker's lease: a
subtraction, ordered, needing no quorum (drafter's choice); an applied Route ends the orchestrator's round. Both seal; a
void route ends nothing. Without it every node runs to its TTL. It reverses in effect "the principal cannot end its own
round" at a workflow node (C3).

text.tspan: Finding 7 · without write-once attributes, the orchestrator loops for ever

svg.text: Under M_REWRITE a worker that flips its outcome after its node ended lets a route be decided while it reads ok, voided
at apply when it reads bad, and decided again. Each void is ordered, so the log grows without bound: an unbounded
run reached depth 665 after thirteen hours with its queue still level. Settled guards bound how much work the
re-check can be made to do.

text.tspan: §8 · A route is checked again where it is applied, and §9 · completion is not success

svg.text: The race the second check closes (§8): one replica decides, the route commits at a log position, every replica applies it there (ADR-0033 §4)
One replica decides Route(e1): the orchestrator's lease live, epoch and fence current, the
workflow running, the decision point not consumed, and e1 enabled.
The route carries its basis, the log index of the attribute state the orchestrator was shown.
Against s, from a correlator, or the cell Observer's late one: coverage does not stop it,
because it lands after coverage (§7).
found moves from false to true: the guard's read set has moved towards disabled, and
only that way.
Every replica runs the mechanism checks again. e1 is no longer enabled: a finding
against its source. The route is void: ordered, recorded, without effect.
After a void the decision point stays open; the orchestrator may route again while its
lease is live, and if no chosen edge remains enabled the decision point fails.
log index 103
log index 104
log index 105
The finding is not overtaken. FindingPrecedesNoRoute holds over all 106,199 states, and the witness NeverVoidedByFinding is reached with
coverage in force (§7).
The workflow continues past a node the finding was meant to stop: ADR-0033 §4's revocation race. TLC: M_DECIDEONLY breaks
AppliedRouteEnabled, FindingPrecedesNoRoute and OneRoutePerDecision, and nothing else (3,237,513 states).

text.tspan: At decide, and again at apply, a route needs (§8)

svg.text: the orchestrator's lease live, epoch and fence current ∧ the workflow running ∧ the decision point not consumed ∧ the edge enabled: its source ended and covered, its guard true, the routing rule satisfied, no finding
against its source or any ancestor

Because guards are settled (§4), only subtractive events can make that false between the two: a finding, a revocation or lapse, a fence, the workflow ending, or another Route consuming the decision point first.
One route per decision point. A Byzantine orchestrator may send two; the first to apply consumes the decision point and the second is void (M_NOCONSUME).

A route carries its basis. Safety does not need it, since the choice is havoc over enabled edges; forensics does: an Observer and a replay can see what the orchestrator was shown. With settled guards, basis and apply
agree on every attribute a guard reads (BasisStable).
Computed edges never go stale: decided and applied in one step (§3).

A lapsed orchestrator takes no default edge. Its lease ends with the decision point open, and the decision point fails. An edge taken on a timeout would be a grant made by a timeout, which ADR-0024 §2 forbids (
M_DEFAULT). A Byzantine orchestrator can stall a workflow and cannot misroute it.

text.tspan: §9 · The mechanism decides completion, and completion is not success

svg.text: Completes when every sink has ended or been skipped and at least one has ended. Fails when a node fails, a decision point fails, a grant is refused, the epoch is fenced, or T_wf or the step bound passes. A timeout is
always a failure (M_TIMEOUTDONE).

Completion says the graph was traversed, not that the work is right. Whether it is right is an Observer finding, deny-only, as ever. A workflow's failure stops nothing else: every lease ends by its own path, and no
other workflow is touched.

text.tspan: §5–§7 · Labels cross cells along the edges; lineages alternate where content is read in the clear; an edge waits for coverage
Proposed · ADR-0043 A3 · ADR-0047 A1 · ADR-0035 R8 · ADR-0039 A3
§5 · A worker's output is the next node's input ⟨K9⟩

svg.text: Run's ingress (ADR-0043 §1) gains a fifth item, input: a predecessor's output, delivered to a node along an edge. The list
stays closed (ADR-0043 A3; C2).
Its label is the reporting worker's clearSet at the Report's emit. clearSet only grows, so this is the sound bound
ADR-0047 §1 already uses for a literal: whatever the worker read in the clear before writing may be in what it wrote. Not
declared (ADR-0047 A1).
Its delivery mode is the edge's, and the receiving bundle's table may only narrow it, clear to handle (ADR-0041 A4 §5).
A task slot takes a handle; the task's label is the template's joined with every handle's in it.

text.tspan: R5 to R7 follow content across cells

svg.text: An item delivered clear joins the receiver's clearSet, so the label forbids bind downstream: an untrusted read at s
delivered clear to b makes b's outward call face R5 to R7.
That is the path ADR-0051 finding 2 says the floor cannot see between two cells; along a workflow's own edges it now can.
Not covered: an injection that changes what a worker says in a Report (ToO §2.10). The workflow makes that gap carry
weight, because the Report now travels. The label bounds where it can go, not what it says.
(drafter's choice: the routing analogue of R6) An edge whose target's lease reaches an outward entry, or receives

text.tspan: input, is disabled when any attribute its guard reads is labelled

svg.text: An attribute's label is its source's: the node's label for every attribute, because a declared outcome was chosen by a worker
that read what its label says; observed ones are kept at the same label for simplicity (drafter's choice).
Finding 6: the label of outcome is coarse. A workflow that touches untrusted content early may find its outward edges
disabled for the rest of the graph. That is the rule working, and it will be felt.
For every clear edge u→v, u's and v's Thinker Personas satisfy ADR-0035's independence rule, E1 to E5; within every
cell Thinker and Observer are independent. A handle edge carries no bytes, and diversity on it buys nothing.
With two lineages the Thinkers along clear edges alternate and each Observer takes the other: the archetype's two
(ADR-0017), enough for any workflow whose clear edges are bipartite.
Enforced at the promotion tally, where refusal stalls (ADR-0035 R8). ADR-0035 is Proposed, so it cannot be enforced

text.tspan: yet: every deployment today declares D-0054-1.

svg.text: Open (finding 5): must parallel branches a join compares in the clear differ from each other?

text.tspan: §7 · An edge waits for its source's coverage (ADR-0039 A3)

svg.text: ADR-0039 §2 grants a Thinker's next round only once a cell Observer has read its last round to the seal. An edge is the workflow's next round, so it is enabled only when its source's covered is true, and a
cell Observer's finding lands before any successor runs.

It does not close §8's race: a correlator's finding, or a cell Observer's late one, may still be ordered after coverage. M_UNCOVERED breaks only EdgeAfterCoverage, and FindingPrecedesNoRoute still holds
without coverage: the re-check is what holds it.
Cost: a node's Observer's lag, at every step of a workflow (Consequences).
§10 · Degeneracy on this record (the record's table)
Declaration
Lineage alternation on clear edges: enforced at the tally → declared.
Every deployment today, since ADR-0035 is Proposed
A clear edge joins independent lineages
None. Alternation is not a conjunct of Contained
Deployment
Coverage at the edge: required → waived, for a deployment whose Run
budget cannot wait for a node's Observer to reach the seal
An edge is enabled only after its source is covered
None. §8 still voids a route on a finding; a finding that lands after the successor starts stops
only what follows

Turning every edge to handle is not a degeneracy: it narrows, and it makes §6 vacuous. At the reference lineage is a declared tag compared at load (I49 (b); no independence table, G18), and D-0054-2 is not built.

svg.text: The floor in force is emergency (28 policies, 107 cases), genesis-provisional. Nothing ratified loads workflow: it is in force only with ADR-0054 and ADR-0041 A4.
The reference links it, at the custodian's direction (2026.10.08), so the floor the reference follows is not the floor in force. Every Run request lifts decisionPoint.

Columns, in order: AppliedRouteEnabled; OneRoutePerDecision; FindingPrecedesNoRoute; ChosenOnlyByRoute; EdgeAfterCoverage; TaintedNeverOutward; GrantUnderPromotion; PromotedAlternates; CompletedOnlyBySink; BasisStable. Each mutation breaks the property it is about, and every mutation is shown to break nothing else: M_DECIDEONLY

three, M_NOCONSUME two, the rest one each. M_UNCOVERED breaks only EdgeAfterCoverage: without coverage FindingPrecedesNoRoute still holds, which is §7's claim that coverage does not close the race and the re-check does. The one bounded row: under M_REWRITE the log has no bound (finding 7), so its remainder is checked under the state constraint CapLog (idx ≤ 6),
the furthest the unmutated module reaches, by the custodian's decision (R2).

The tenth witness's partner: LogReach (idx ≤ 6) holds over all 106,199 states with no mutation, so the cap's justification is in the results and not in a probe. spec/Workflow-results-2026.10.08.txt: 33 rows from Workflow-rows.txt, TLC 2.19.

There is no proof module. Proofs of the ten properties are an open obligation (ADR-0054 §12 "Not met"; Open obligations), and spec/proof-sync.sh
exits 1 for want of a reason (G11 item 101). No binding row in theorem-premise-binding.md (item 90).
Model: Nodes = {s, b, c, j}, lineages {A, B}, one fence; orchestrator and workers havoc. Not modelled: more than one decision point; multi-select; all
joins and skips; the orchestrator's own seating and rounds; Run admits inside a round; attestation at grant; the step and time bounds; erasure. Deadlock
is not checked: a workflow may stall, and stalling is safe.
R1: the module was corrected twice before the rows were kept (M_NOCONSUME once skipped decide too; a stale route could re-activate a node). Freezes
at ADR-0054's ratification (G11 §3).

text.tspan: At the reference: built to a Proposed record, on a floor not in force (ADR-0033 A16, A17, both pending)
Built at reference · A16 · A17 pending
A workflow is a promoted artifact, and a malformed one does not load

svg.text: WorkflowLoad takes the text of a single-file workspace and loads it only if that workspace's artifact was promoted by tally, as a profile is. A dag with a cycle, a mesh with no budget, an orchestrator without a chosen edge or a chosen edge without one, a
guard reading a node that does not dominate its source, a seating whose kind or alphabet is wrong, and a clear edge with one declared lineage on both ends do not load
workflow.rs (18): a_workflow_loads_only_promoted_and_well_formed,
a_mesh_loads_only_with_a_budget_and_two_coloured_clear_edges; e2e a_workflow_is_run_by_its_promotion, step 1

WorkflowGrant: a replica's driver proposes the grant of each ready slot, a node's activation or an orchestrator's decision event, served in log order; apply rebuilds the request from the seating and requires equality, with the task's label joined with the clear
inputs'. A refusal by the budget or a grant check fails the slot; a fence fails what is not yet granted
a_fence_fails_a_node_not_yet_granted; e2e steps 3, 4, 6, 7

An orchestrator seat holds Route and Report. A route is stamped with its workflow, event and basis, checked at decide and again at apply, and void if it fails: the round is the event's, the event not consumed, the edge chosen and enabled. An applied
route consumes the event, enters its target and ends the round. A computed edge is evaluated once, inside the apply that makes it evaluable
a_route_applies_and_the_workflow_completes_by_its_sink,
a_route_decided_before_a_finding_and_applied_after_is_void, a_second_route_to_a_consumed_decision_point_is_void,

svg.text: A clear input's label joins the receiver's clearSet at grant, and the floor's R5 then binds its outward call. An edge into an outward node, or one carrying restricted content in the clear, is disabled by an untrusted attribute its guard reads
an_untrusted_attribute_disables_the_edge_into_an_outward_node, a_clear_input_joins_the_receivers_clear_set;

text.tspan: Activations, causal history, the budget; the mechanism tracks

svg.text: One engine for both kinds: each node run is an activation with its trigger and causal history; a guard reads the history and never a node's latest value; a finding closes every edge downstream; every lease is charged, orchestrator rounds included; one
orchestrator round per event, told the track and never bytes (the mesh: D6)

text.tspan: is the one count a guard compares"

svg.text: Attributes loses denials and Counter loses Denials, so a guard that names a denial count does not parse and no attribute is lifted as 0. A denial is still written to the round topic and still not ordered; the correlator and the Observer read it there
workflow.rs (18), unchanged; the whole suite

A16: mechanism/ and policies/ at 11aaf6a, manifest SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.08 (116 entries, 9357abd49333459a), on the workflow stage; 155 tests across fifteen binaries, up from 133 (eighteen in topak-core/tests/workflow.rs, three in topak-floor/tests/workflow.rs, one e2e); the Rego tests A15's 38, unchanged. A17: 749d54f, SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.09 (809c66beda3cdc6a), three entries changed, 155 tests, none failing. Seen at the replicated state, not end to end, all but one: the e2e run shows the four-node

workflow promoted, loaded and run across three replicas by scripted cells (a computed edge on a typed attribute, a route admitted by R8, a second route refused, completion by the sink). Nothing in force is discharged.
(a) PROVISIONAL (finding-record): no record fixes a finding's form; the shape is a heartbeat's, and only workflows read it.
(b) PROVISIONAL (workflow-lineage): a tag the text declares, compared on every clear edge at load (D-0054-1).
(c) PROVISIONAL (workflow-rung0): a seating above rung 0 does not load; the grant carries no appraisal.
(d) PROVISIONAL (workflow-mesh-joins): an all join in a mesh does not load.
(e) PROVISIONAL (workflow-handles): a handle input is labelled and recorded, and cannot be resolved by the guest.
(f) PROVISIONAL (workflow-inputs): a clear input comes from the cache of the replica that wrote the reports; another delivers
none (finding 23).
(g) PROVISIONAL (workflow-occupant): sessions handed out by WorkflowStatus, a BOOTSTRAP standing in for a launch
per slot; the cells are the tests', not ADR-0036's occupant.
(h) an input's label is the reporter's clearSet at its seal, not at each emit: coarser, and sound.
(i) outward is the text's declaration joined with the deciding replica's reading of the bundle.

text.tspan: The delivery table's narrowing of an edge's mode.

svg.text: Seatings above rung 0.
21 · A round that ends on its own admit seals after that admit's record. The seal came before the deciding replica wrote
the ending record, which was then refused as sealed; fixed (seal_round). ADR-0042 §5 says when a lease ends, not that the
seal follows the ending admit's record, and A3 makes the case new.
22 · denials had no replicated source. The reference lifted 0 at first. Closed by ADR-0054 R6, 2026.10.09.
23 · A clear input needs a read path the reference does not have: the transport writes topics and does not read them. The
record's delivery is right; the reference needs a topic read path (ADR-0005) or a replicated store of outputs to follow it after a
failover.

svg.text: Trace validation was not rerun: spec/Mechanism.tla does not model workflows, and a traced run that loads one would not
match it; WorkflowLoad and WorkflowGrant are projected by name. Stage one of the refinement chain is behind the tree.
mechanism/lean is stale: SeatsModel.lean and CouplingModel.lean transcribe ActionKind and SeatKind, which
gained Route and orchestrator; tools/lean-sync.sh exits 1. Left so by the custodian's decision of 2026.10.08.

text.tspan: is tied to the reference by tests named after its properties, and by no trace.
Ten dependent amendments, drafted 2026.10.08 and pending (ADR-0054 R3; G11 §1.1)

svg.text: Route is a principal emission
The Decision gains a paragraph: Route(edge) is admitted, ordered and recorded on its round topic, so it is an emission; the lease it leads to is granted under the workflow's promotion, which is
the authority change. Both sets stay at two
C2 marking; finding 3
A workflow is a set of seatings and a graph
§1: the nodes are seatings voted on with the graph; the tally is the authority for every lease; the mechanism grants each when its node becomes ready, nothing wider than the seating; a refused
grant fails the node; a rules-epoch change voids leases not yet issued; the tally checks lineage alternation on clear edges. §2's quorum rule and the gates unchanged
A third grant path: a workflow's node
§2: the node's lease is granted under the workflow's tally; appraised and refused as any grant; a refusal fails the node; no operator makes successor grants inside a workflow, while its denies
reach every cell; one live lease per principal orders a principal's rounds. §1's field set and §4's monotonicity unchanged
C1: every worker's grant travels it
A seat kind orchestrator
§4's table gains it: Run only, Route and Report, no authoring variant; seated by a workflow's promotion, one round per decision point, coupled to its Observer. The kinds are six. B10 binds it by
kind as written
Coverage at a workflow's edge, and the orchestrator coupled
§2: an edge out of a node is enabled only when a cell Observer has read its round to the seal; it subtracts and closes no race, which §8's re-check does; an orchestrator seat's admits need
live(o); waiving it is D-0054-2
A fourth variant, Route, and an early end
§1: Route(edge), held only by an orchestrator seat, a principal emission, its envelope a chosen edge out of the lease's decision point; "exactly three" reads "exactly four". §3: R counts it. §4: a
worker's Report carrying outcome ends its lease, and an applied Route ends the orchestrator's round, with no terminal variant. §6: three obligations and their owners
C3: the alphabet gains a variant
Route's envelope
§1: R8-route-own-decision and R9-only-orchestrators-route; R3 scoped to thinker and orchestrator, covering Route; B10 unchanged; enabledness stays a mechanism check. §4: S
names Route over a Seat and an Edge. §5: an input in the edge's mode, which a bundle may only narrow; an orchestrator's delivery table a mechanism constant. Its Cedar text is the workflow
stage (R3)
Two more ends of a round
§5's table gains the admit of a worker's Report carrying outcome at a workflow node, and the apply of an orchestrator's Route; both seal. "The principal cannot end its own round" is narrowed at a
workflow node; still no terminal variant and no release
C3: reverses that sentence in effect
A fifth item, input, and the orchestrator's Listener
§1: a predecessor's output reaches a node along an edge, labelled by the reporter's clearSet at emit, in the edge's mode or narrower, joining the receiver's clearSet when clear; task slots take
handles; the list stays closed. The orchestrator's own closed list, never bytes. §2: an orchestrator row, Route and Report
C2: the ingress list gains an item
The label of an input; the attributes; the routing rule
§1: an input is labelled by the reporting worker's clearSet at emit, with no declaration. §4: the fixed set of mechanism-computed attributes gains a node's, denials struck ⟨R6⟩, read by guards
and never by policy, each at its node's label, outcome declared; an edge into an outward or restricted-receiving node is disabled when a guard reads an untrusted attribute
finding 6
Lineages alternate at a workflow's tally
A revision in place of a Proposed record, not an amendment: for every clear edge the two Thinkers' Personas are independent by the table, and every cell's Thinker and Observer are; handle
edges are not checked; declared, not enforced, until ADR-0035 is ratified. No exclusion rule in §3 changes
D-0054-1; finding 5

Each is marked inline and not applied, with a History row in its record: "Pending — drafted 2026.10.08 by the assistant at the custodian's direction, not reviewed. Takes force only with ADR-0054's ratification." With ADR-0033 A16 and A17 they are G11's twelve pending amendments, every one depending on a Proposed record. Two go past
§12's list where the decision needs them: ADR-0043 A3's Run-table row and ADR-0039 A3's coupling (R3).
Met ⟨R3⟩: the ten above and ADR-0035 R8

text.tspan: A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)

svg.text: The workflow interpreter, the guard evaluator and the orchestrator's Listener table are part of the mechanism, under ADR-0045's existing mechanism row, because every decision
they make subtracts or executes a grant the quorum made. More verified code on the path every Run grant now travels.
Findings (ADR-0054, the record's seven)
Run had no path between cells. ADR-0043's ingress list is closed and names no other cell; "cells communicate through the record" was true only of Build

The orchestrator's safety argument needs nothing from the orchestrator. It may only narrow, so every property is stated over enabled edges; it is in the record for quality alone, which is why it is optional
Route strains ADR-0015's enumeration: ordered and recorded like an emission, its consequence a grant. The record puts the grant on the promotion; a C2 reviewer may read it as a third kind

Settled guards are what make the re-check cheap. Write-once attributes and dominator read sets remove any difference between what the orchestrator was shown and the state at apply that no subtraction explains; M_REWRITE shows the difference
Two parallel branches of one lineage can agree by a shared blind spot. Whether the branches of a compare-and-merge must differ, which needs three lineages at a three-way merge, is open

The label of outcome is coarse. One untrusted read labels every attribute a worker produces, so an honest workflow may lose its outward edges for the rest of the graph. The routing rule working, and it will be felt
Without write-once attributes the orchestrator can loop for ever ⟨R2⟩: decided, voided, decided again, each void ordered; depth 665 after thirteen hours

text.tspan: What it costs, and what is still open (Consequences; Open obligations; G11 item 101)

svg.text: Many principals: each node is a cell with its own Observer, on its own device, of the other lineage; n nodes and an orchestrator are about 2n+2 principals.
A worker steers the routing through its declared outcome, within the enabled edges.
A non-bipartite pattern of clear edges cannot be seated with two lineages: it fails the tally at the archetype, or declares D-0054-1.
It rests on four Proposed or provisional records: ADR-0035, ADR-0050, ADR-0024 A3 and ADR-0047's attributes.
Open: proofs; all joins, skips and multi-select in the module; values for T_wf and the step bound; finding 5; a per-attribute label; correlations over workflows for ADR-0051 (G11
item 97); binding rows; the custodian's reading of every drafter's choice.
